title_fa: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
excerpt_en: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came...
excerpt_fa: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came...
content_en:
After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.
Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.
News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge...

News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge...

content_en:
I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.
The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy
I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.
Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.
In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive
What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.
Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.
Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally
One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?
Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. It is an altered picture of Trump himself, taken after a failed assassination attempt in 2024. Trump’s head has been replaced with Jensen Huang’s head. The...

title_en: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
title_fa: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
excerpt_en: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.
excerpt_fa: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.
content_en:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

title_en: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
title_fa: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
excerpt_en: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
excerpt_fa: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
content_en:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.
Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.
Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.
“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.
The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.
The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.
Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.
Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.
Supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.
For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.
Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.
“We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”
“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.
Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.
“We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being said, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.
To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.
“We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”
Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders said they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.
Mignano, meanwhile, says he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.
With the new funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. Mignano and Murr are in New York, while Peterson is in the Austin area but commutes to New York at times. The team says it hopes to figure out a...

title_en: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
title_fa: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
excerpt_en: "The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk chimed in.
excerpt_fa: "The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk chimed in.
content_en:
A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.
“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.
Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.
“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”
Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.
In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.
“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.”
Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the company he founded after scandals, also voiced his support for Huang on X.
When Nvidia’s stock tanked in reaction to Huang’s ousting, billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said he believes that the Nvidia board was “not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.” As Nvidia’s stock began to rebound Monday morning, Ackman wrote, “The wisdom of the crowd prevails.”
The attitude toward Huang’s return is not as celebratory outside of the tech industry. Across the political spectrum, some elected officials are skeptical about President Donald Trump’s claims that Huang’s return does not threaten national security.
“No national security risk? Based on what?” wrote Senator John Cornyn (R-TX).
Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NB) added, “Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress. It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”
Huang is still expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.

title_en: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
title_fa: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
excerpt_en: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.
excerpt_fa: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.
content_en:
Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.
The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”
Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.
TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

title_en: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
title_fa: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks

excerpt_fa: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It's a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic...
content_en:
The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.
AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.
Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.
Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”
To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit.
Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice).
With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever.
To meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside.
Meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency.
“That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event.
In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found.
To stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation.
Many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build new sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall.
“Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”
“In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”
There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports.
Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. title_en: Your older, discontinued AirTags can still serve a purpose
title_fa: Your older, discontinued AirTags can still serve a purpose
excerpt_en: Apple has moved on from the original AirTag, but you don't have to. Find out how your old trackers can still earn their keep at home and on the go.
excerpt_fa: Apple has moved on from the original AirTag, but you don't have to. Find out how your old trackers can still earn their keep at home and on the go.
content_en:
Your older, discontinued AirTags can still serve a purpose
Before you toss your original AirTag, here are a few ways to keep it useful.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Earlier this year, Apple introduced the first new generation AirTag since the original debuted in 2021. And while you might still be able to find first-generation Apple AirTags for purchase on some websites, Apple doesn't sell them anymore. The company is now focusing solely on the new model and leaving the original AirTag behind. But the old ones are still supported in the Find My app, so there's lots of ways you can continue to use them.
The newer Apple AirTag offers an expanded finding range thanks to the second-generation ultrawideband chip, upgraded Bluetooth chip, improved Precision Finding from up to 50 percent farther away and a louder speaker. Given how cheap Apple AirTags are ($29 on Amazon) and all the upgrades with the second-gen model, you'll probably want to grab a few for your most precious items.
But that doesn't mean you should toss your old AirTags. They can be relocated to secondary items, kept as backups for your most important gear or handed down to friends and family.
Use them for secondary items
An AirTag that still works is worth hanging onto. Use newer AirTags for your keys, purse, wallet, child's backpack and maybe even pet collar and move your old AirTags to secondary items. Toss one in your glove compartment or trunk of your car in case of theft or to keep track of your newly licensed teen if they turn off location sharing in Find My. Or put one in your luggage as a secondary method of tracking its location if it's lost or misplaced.
Keep one in your child's jacket pocket so they're still trackable if they don't have their backpack (some parents even stitch them into their kids' shoes). Clip one secondary set of keys you often misplace in the house, like the key to the back door or home office filing cabinet. While the range is farther and the speaker louder on the new AirTag, both are still sufficient on the older model for finding items within the home. My son used Precision Finding with an old AirTag the other day to locate his house keys and it worked perfectly well.
You could also get creative and affix one to the inside of your headphones case or toss one in your dressy purse, clutch or wallet so you don't have to move the new AirTag back and forth when you switch. Or keep one with items that are tough to find in a cluttered space, like holiday decorations in the attic, a toolbox in the garage or a small remote in the game room. AirTags use easily replaceable CR2032 batteries that last about a year with normal usage and under normal conditions.
Other things you can do with an old AirTag
Since the new Precision Finding benefits of the second-generation Apple AirTag are only supported with iPhone 15 and newer models, you won't be able to use one if you have an older phone. In this case, it's still worthwhile to continue using a first-gen Apple AirTag until you upgrade your phone. Standard Precision Finding works with iPhone 11 through 14 models, so consider handing over the old AirTag to a friend or family member with an older iPhone, like a parent or grandparent. They can use it for their wallet, purse, eyeglasses case or other item they often misplace.
If you want to be extra diligent, use a second older AirTag with a new battery as a backup in case the battery in your new AirTag dies before you get the chance to replace it. A second AirTag can also add security. Think putting the new AirTag under your bicycle seat and the older one under the bike's bottle cage or inside the bell. A thief might find one and dispose of it, but likely won't find both.
Some buyback sites in certain countries also purchase old AirTags. While Apple doesn't accept AirTags for trade-in, sites like Sell Techs in the UK and BuyBackWorld do. So you could make a bit of cash by selling them. Just because older AirTags are slowly becoming obsolete, that doesn't mean they don't still have their use.

title_en: New leaks reveal the iPhone 18e will have a redesigned camera plateau
title_fa: New leaks reveal the iPhone 18e will have a redesigned camera plateau
excerpt_en: We've also got further confirmation the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera lens.
excerpt_fa: We've also got further confirmation the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera lens.
content_en:
New leaks reveal the iPhone 18e will have a redesigned camera plateau
We've also got further confirmation the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera.
Apple seems to have adopted a new strategy for the iPhone launch, splitting it into two phases. After launching the premium iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo in September, Apple is preparing new versions of the lower-priced models — and it looks like they'll look a lot more like the more expensive iPhones. CAD images of the new iPhone 18e seen by Engadget show a redesigned camera bump on the back of the phone, similar to the one on the Pro models. The images come from a source familiar with Apple's supply chain who who had previously shared accurate tips on the colors of the iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro before they were announced.
The current iPhone 17e doesn't have a camera bump — instead, the lens has a small protrusion and sits flush against the back of the phone, with the microphone and LED flash also embedded in cutouts directly in the rear glass. But according to CAD images seen by Engadget, Apple appears to be considering changing that with the iPhone 18e. The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone. It's somewhat similar to the camera module on the M5 iPad Pro (which you can see in the image below).
Interestingly, it seems that the iPhone 18e will be the only model to feature this new camera plateau. The same files include the CADs for the base iPhone 18 and the iPhone Air 2, both of which are expected to launch alongside the 18e next spring. The base iPhone 18 will keep the exact same design, but now with a thicker camera module — increasing from 3.45mm (0.14 inches) to 3.8mm (0.15 inches). Apple has been using the same 48-megapixel Sony IMX904 sensor for its base models since the iPhone 15, so a thicker camera module could mean new sensors or upgraded cameras.
As for the iPhone Air 2, the CADs seen by Engadget corroborate previous rumors that Apple's ultra-thin phone will feature a second rear camera — not a surprise given that its single lens was one of the main complaints about it. Although the Air 2 will remain 5.6mm thick, the camera module will increase in thickness from 3.45mm (0.14 inches) to 3.8mm (0.15 inches), with the two lenses aligned horizontally. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the leaker Digital Chat Station and analyst Jeff Pu have all said Apple is adding an ultra-wide lens to the second-generation Air, and the CAD images back those reports up.
Also, the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are expected to keep the same Dynamic Island as current models rather than the smaller cutout on the iPhone 18 Pro. Of course, these changes may end up being scrapped and never see the light of day, since Apple still has some time before they hit the stores next year.

As for the iPhone Air 2, the CADs seen by Engadget corroborate previous rumors that Apple's ultra-thin phone will feature a second rear camera — not a surprise given that its single lens was one of the main complaints about it. Although the Air 2 will remain 5.6mm thick, the camera module will increase in thickness from 3.45mm (0.14 inches) to 3.8mm (0.15 inches), with the two lenses aligned horizontally. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the leaker Digital Chat Station and analyst Jeff Pu have all said Apple is adding an ultra-wide lens to the second-generation Air, and the CAD images back those reports up.
Also, the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are expected to keep the same Dynamic Island as current models rather than the smaller cutout on the iPhone 18 Pro. Of course, these changes may end up being scrapped and never see the light of day, since Apple still has some time before they hit the stores next year.

title_en: GTA 6 player gets social ban on PSN after sending a photo of in-game nudity
title_fa: GTA 6 player gets social ban on PSN after sending a photo of in-game nudity
excerpt_en: Apparently just because it's in the game doesn't mean sharing "obscene" content is okay.
excerpt_fa: Apparently just because it's in the game doesn't mean sharing "obscene" content is okay.
content_en:
GTA 6 player gets social ban on PSN after sending a photo of in-game nudity
Apparently just because it’s in the game doesn’t mean sharing “obscene” content is okay.
Grand Theft Auto 6 has dominated everyone's attention since it came out last week and broke the record for the most day one retail sales in entertainment history. Unfortunately, not everyone's experience has been 100 percent positive, especially now that one player has been hit with a social ban on PSN after sharing a photo of naked people taken with the game's built-in camera feature.
According to X user @derrickgott007, they received a notice from PlayStation Safety saying their account was being temporarily suspended from using social features for 30 days after breaching the company's code of conduct regarding pornographic or obscene content. The issue is that the user claims the offending image was actually a photo taken using GTA 6's camera feature of a nudist resort they found inside the game before sharing it with someone else on PSN.
In this case, if you simply go by what's outlined in PlayStation's code of conduct, technically this player did break the rules as there's a specific bullet point about not sharing, soliciting, accessing, distributing or storing "material that is obscene, pornographic, or illegal." However, where things get a bit murky is that the source of the offending material came from a game being played on a PS5 that is also sold digitally by Sony itself. This feels a bit hypocritical as it seems that it's okay for a game to contain nudity or pornographic material, but as soon as you take a photo or screenshot of said content, suddenly you're in violation of PlayStation's guidelines.
Furthermore, while a social ban might not sound that bad as the user will still have access to some games, because online multiplayer falls under the umbrella of social activity, @derrickgott007 says they can't even play Call of Duty during their 30-day suspension.
Another interesting topic that incidents like this bring up is how often regular people agree to things they haven't fully read or acknowledged due to a company's terms of service (ToS) or end-user license agreement (EULA). Often, these documents are so long and onerous that people blindly skip past them and hit the checkbox just so they can use the thing they paid for. Some organizations like the ToS;DR project have made efforts to call out companies with terms of services that are unnecessarily dense or difficult to understand, but it remains an ongoing issue for almost everyone in modern society.
Sadly, even though PlayStation's guidelines seem a bit contradictory, this incident should serve as a public service announcement to anyone considering taking a photo or screenshot of potentially obscene material in GTA 6 (or other games) with their PS5, as they need to be extra careful or else they risk getting hit with a similar ban.

title_en: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
title_fa: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
excerpt_en: "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," Huang told employees.
excerpt_fa: "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," Huang told employees.
content_en:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.
The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”
Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”
Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

title_en: Grand Theft Auto 6 is really about the death of the American Dream
title_fa: Grand Theft Auto 6 is really about the death of the American Dream
excerpt_en: The struggle in GTA6 is both real and virtual.
excerpt_fa: The struggle in GTA6 is both real and virtual.
content_en:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is really about the death of the American Dream
The struggle is both real and virtual.
Even when they were well written, every GTA story has ultimately been about solving your problems with the accumulation of wealth. But Grand Theft Auto 6 specifically focuses on the systemic issues that make any version of the American Dream — saving money, buying a home and supporting a family with a fulfilling job — incredibly difficult for people living on the margins of society. The crushing weight of capitalism is always pressing down on you, just like in the real world.
Lucia Caminos committed an ill-conceived robbery, is subsequently sent to jail and is forced to claw her way back into civilian life with little support. Jason Duval joined the Army to escape his troubled youth and ends up serving as muscle for a small-time criminal. Much like the real Bonnie and Clyde, Lucia and Jason are driven by the need to escape poverty, but it's up to you to determine if they'll share a similar end.
I only have around 12 hours of GTA 6 under my belt so far (it's estimated to take around 50 hours to beat, and hundreds of hours to fully complete), but Rockstar clearly frames why our lead characters pursue a life of crime: beyond the generational poverty and lack of upward mobility, Lucia and Jason are also trying to build enough stability to reclaim custody of their infant son.
When she decides to stick up a payday loan store (the existence of which is inherently predatory against low-income people), she's doing it to feed her kid, afford diapers and survive as a single mother. (Jason isn't aware of him at that point in the story.) It's hard to imagine Lucia making such a desperate decision if she had enough social support. But of course, that's not the American way.
Six months worth of baby formula costs upwards of $2,700 in the US,, whereas it's just $759 in the UK. And while America ranks fifth when it comes to the affordability of diapers changes worldwide, that's still around $1,200 a year — a significant cost for poor families. Lucia is lucky that her infant son is placed into kinship care with her aunt, instead of general foster care. Many kinship caregivers receive foster stipends to support their charges, and fostered children also receive Medicaid for free and low-cost healthcare. Ironically, biological parents don't get automatic state support for their kids, and Medicaid eligibility depends on the family's income.
Jason has his own problems. He left the Army after unspecified "trouble" and later worked for a low-grade private security firm. Given his testy relationship to the military, he says he can't receive any veteran home loan benefits, and that may also extend to other assistance, like employment transition and healthcare. He learns that it's easier to use the skills he's gained from the military as a tool for criminal violence, instead of following a more acceptable path like construction. He recommits to Lucia while she's in prison, and GTA 6 begins with him learning that she's about to be released with close supervision. (She's getting out not because of any legal changes in her case, but because her women's prison is too full.)
Jason gets to work rebuilding a small seaside home on loan from his criminal boss (played by the great character actor Stephen Root). It's clear he can put up drywall and nail down roof tiles. But even as he prepares for a more domestic life, he's pulled deeper into the criminal underworld. It gets him some extra cash, but it also makes him a less suitable caregiver for the son he's never met.
After Jason brings Lucia home from jail, it becomes all the more clear how difficult their life is going to be. GTA 6 centers heavily on their relationship (doing things like fixing up the house early on earns Lucia's favor, to the anger of online incels). But love won't be enough if they can't find a way to survive legitimately and build a safe home for their son. They can't even open a bank account, thanks to their poor credit scores. Instead, they're pushed towards a slimy Zelle/Venmo clone called BuckMe, which is specifically targeted at poor people.
It takes several hours before you can even use BuckMe or ATMs, though — until then, you're stuck hiding money under your floorboards. Jason is wise enough to start a small family fund, but it could all easily be lost if their home is robbed or destroyed (something to consider for later in the game.) GTA 6 is stricter towards players when it comes to money than previous entries in the series: You lose everything you're carrying if you're killed or arrested. If you have a run-in with the cops or some baddies after a big job, it could end up being a tremendous loss.
"Everything is corrupt and rotten," Lucia says as she tries to convince Jason to hang out with her rich friends, who may be able to send more lucrative criminal work their way. "The only thing that matters is who you know and what you've got." It's a bleak point of view that might resonate with anyone who's observed the last decade of grift-driven American politics. Lucia's version of the American Dream is built on idolizing rich people living on luxury yachts and flaunting their ill-gotten wealth on social media. If society doesn't deem you worthy enough to even have a bank account, why abide by its rules?
You could try to strike it rich by robbing stores, banks and people on the street, but GTA 6's voluminous amounts of voice acting and complex character animation almost makes the prospect of random violence uncomfortably real. Sticking up a retail clerk feels bad, because you and the cashier you're aiming a gun at are both ultimately struggling to get by in an unfair country ruled by grifters. (I haven't seen the people in charge yet, but there are plenty of Trumpian parallels in the in-game right-wing TV channel Weasel.) If you try to jack the wrong car, you might get someone crashing out about how difficult their life is. Everybody hurts,...

title_en: Anthropic softens its data retention policy for Mythos and Fable model use
title_fa: Anthropic softens its data retention policy for Mythos and Fable model use
excerpt_en: Enterprise customers can now keep prompts and responses on their own servers.
excerpt_fa: Enterprise customers can now keep prompts and responses on their own servers.
content_en:
Anthropic softens its data retention policy for Mythos and Fable model use
Enterprise customers can now keep prompts and responses on their own servers.
Anthropic is making a major change to its policy involving the use of its Mythos and Fable models. Back when the company first debuted version 5 of those AI systems in June, it said it would retain any user prompts and responses generated by the models for 30 days to ensure they were not being misused.
That policy was not popular among Anthropic's enterprise customers, even after the company said it would not enforce a similar requirement for the latest version of its Opus model. Anthropic eventually identified its stance as a risk factor to its success, particularly if other AI providers adopted so-called "zero data retention" policies. As predicted, that's exactly what happened, with OpenAI announcing its own ZDR implementation in August. Less than a month later, Anthropic revealed it was working on Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a technology it said would combine the privacy of ZDR "with state-of-the-art safeguards for detecting misuse." Per Bloomberg, Anthropic is now rolling out an early version of that system to its business customers.
With EFS, Anthropic will still require those clients to retain prompts and responses for 30 days, but it will instead allow them to store that data on their own servers. Jon Turow, the company's head of safeguards for Mythos and Fable, told Bloomberg that Anthropic would do occasional 15-minute checks to look for signs of potential cyberattacks. If the company's automated systems detect a problem, they'll notify the customer. Anthropic will also get an alert, but Turow said the company would not be able to access related data.
The release arrives following Anthropic's high-profile initial public offering last Thursday. After an exuberant debut, the company's stock is trading for around $86 as of 2:53 PM ET, or just $3 above its original price of $83.

title_en: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3
title_fa: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3
excerpt_en: It's going to be a busy few days in Washington DC for the freshly reinstated CEO.
excerpt_fa: It's going to be a busy few days in Washington DC for the freshly reinstated CEO.
content_en:
NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3
It’s going to be a busy few days in Washington DC for the freshly reinstated CEO.
A week after reclaiming his job as NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Huang will be heading to Washington DC for two hearings in front of lawmakers. It had already been confirmed that Huang will face a trio of House committees on December 1. While that testimony is slated to take place behind closed doors, the Senate Banking Committee will instead grill Huang in a public hearing on December 3. Get the popcorn ready for that one.
In a statement to Bloomberg, committee chair Sen. Tim Scott said the hearing will focus on oversight of US export controls. The committee initially asked Huang to testify after he admitted to an affair. Reports had linked him with an executive at a company to which NVIDIA is said to have sold over $4 billion worth of chips and other equipment. US officials suspect that executive, Alice Huang, of being a Chinese spy.
Since 2024, the US Commerce and Justice departments have been investigating Megaspeed, the Singaporean cloud computing company she worked for between 2023 and 2025. Alice Huang is also reportedly under investigation over alleged links to Chinese AI companies that may have violated US export rules by smuggling in chips from the likes of NVIDIA and Super Micro Computer.
NVIDIA opened its own investigation following reports of the affair. The New York Times later reported he had another affair, this time with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. He resigned from the company the next day, November 12.
On Monday, NVIDIA's board said it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately, after receiving assurances from high-level US officials that bringing him back in wouldn't pose a threat to national security. President Donald Trump (whose investment accounts have traded tens of millions of dollars of NVIDIA stock during his second term) said he convinced the board to reappoint Huang.
NVIDIA last week established an export control compliance committee and on Monday said it was looking to appoint someone in a new position of Chief Compliance Officer. Both the company's investigation and the Banking Committee's probe are ongoing.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat member of the committee, said in a statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement. Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk."
Along with colleagues from both sides of the aisle, Warren is pushing forward legislation that would more tightly restrict NVIDIA exports. The AI Overwatch Act would codify Trump's limitations on chip exports to "foreign adversaries" into law. The Chip Security Act would force NVIDIA and other companies to monitor the locations of chips they send abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would strengthen semiconductor export controls for the US and its allies. According to Bloomberg, final talks are underway to roll these bills into an annual defense package that lawmakers usually pass in December.

title_en: The infamous GTA 6 hacker has been released after pleading guilty
title_fa: The infamous GTA 6 hacker has been released after pleading guilty
excerpt_en: A judge warned the hacker not to "let this happen again."
excerpt_fa: A judge warned the hacker not to "let this happen again."
content_en:
The infamous GTA 6 hacker has been released after pleading guilty
A judge warned not to “let this happen again.”
The hacker who attempted to extort Rockstar Games after grabbing early gameplay clips of GTA 6 has been released, according to a BBC report. Arion Kurtaj was actually sentenced to seven years in prison after pleading guilty but was immediately released on license, which is a provision in the British legal system that lets a person serve their sentence in the community under strict rules instead of behind bars. It's relatively similar to parole or probation in the US.
A judge warned Kurtaj not to "let this happen again" before sending him on his way. He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order that lasts five years. This will restrict his online activity, thus helping to ensure the judge's warning is heeded.
The now 21-year-old was a teenager when he snuck into Rockstar's servers and stole a bunch of data as part of the hacking gang Lapsus$. Kurtaj attempted to extort the company and threatened to release clips of the unfinished game back in 2022. The company didn't relent so he began dropping gameplay clips at regular intervals.
He did all of this in a hotel room with an Amazon Fire Stick while under police protection, as rival hackers had threatened to attack him to get some stolen stashes of Bitcoin. This all sounds like an actual GTA mission, but it's real life.

A leaker called Cyberleek has claimed to have access to an Xbox build of the game that could be used to create a PC port, according to Kotaku.

title_en: ‘Outrageous,’ ‘reckless,’ ‘wow’: Here’s what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
title_fa: ‘Outrageous,’ ‘reckless,’ ‘wow’: Here’s what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
excerpt_en: Politicians on both sides of the aisle seem angry, agitated, and nonplussed by the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia leadership less than two weeks after his ousting.
excerpt_fa: Politicians on both sides of the aisle seem angry, agitated, and nonplussed by the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia leadership less than two weeks after his ousting.
content_en:
Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance with a suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the president posted an AI-generated meme of the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled the famous photo from Trump’s own assassination attempt.
Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affair with Alice Huang may have exposed the company.
Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder may face an uphill battle given the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting with a public Senate appearance scheduled for next week. He is also expected to testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.
If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.

title_en: How to connect your Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X
title_fa: How to connect your Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X
excerpt_en: Connecting Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X can be frustrating due to incompatibility. However, there are a few workarounds to solve this problem.
excerpt_fa: Connecting Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X can be frustrating due to incompatibility. However, there are a few workarounds to solve this problem.
content_en:
How to connect your Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X
Since the Xbox Series consoles lack support for Bluetooth headphones, here's how you can work around the problem.
Having the best audio can elevate any game, and sometimes TV speakers just don't cut it. But while Bluetooth headphones are supported on virtually every device from smartphones to laptops, the same isn't true of game consoles. Out of the box, an Xbox Series X can't connect directly to Bluetooth headphones, but there are a few workarounds if you want to get more out of your game's sound than your TV can provide.
The problem with using even the best wireless Bluetooth headphones for gaming is latency. Sending audio over Bluetooth introduces a tiny delay before your headphones actually receive it. Most of the time, that's not an issue, but when your game's sound is even a fraction of a second off, it can be distracting. Worse, it can make rhythm games that rely on audio cues nearly unplayable. If you do want wireless audio from your Xbox Series X, there are a few solutions, but none are perfect.
How to get around Xbox's lack of Bluetooth
One simple but costly route is to buy the official Xbox Wireless Headset, which retails for $120. Microsoft uses its own wireless standard for these headphones to connect with extremely low latency, and since Bluetooth isn't an option, you have to pay more for the first-party version if you want wireless audio. Some third-party manufacturers like Audeze and SteelSeries also make Xbox-compatible wireless headsets, but they can be just as expensive as Microsoft's version or more. Third-party headsets that support Xbox's wireless protocol need to be licensed by Microsoft, and you'll see the Xbox logo on the box.
Another option is to route Bluetooth audio through an adapter or your TV. Some Bluetooth adapters are made to plug into the Xbox controller's headphone jack and transmit the audio coming through it, while others connect to the console's USB port and transmit from there. Higher-end headphones like the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite that come with a dedicated low-latency dongle are the best choice for sound quality, but they also tend to be more expensive. If you already own a smart TV that can transmit a Bluetooth signal, you can also set your console to output to the TV, then connect it to your headphones. Any of these options will be cheaper than buying an entirely new set of headphones.
The cheapest way to connect your headphones to your Xbox Series X is just to use the controller's audio jack as it's intended. Some Bluetooth headphones include a jack and audio cable as a wired backup, but that's not always the case. If you have any headphones that support wired connections, though, using the controller jack is the best way to avoid latency. It's not actually wireless, of course, but connecting your headphones to the controller won't compromise your audio quality.

title_en: Kodak's SlideTag combines a digital photo frame and an AirTag
title_fa: Kodak's SlideTag combines a digital photo frame and an AirTag
excerpt_en: The SlideTag will come in a blind box with nine fun designs.
excerpt_fa: The SlideTag will come in a blind box with nine fun designs.
content_en:
Kodak's SlideTag combines a digital photo frame and an AirTag
The SlideTag will come in a blind box with nine fun designs.
Kodak is hoping to create another influencer-fueled craze with its latest retro-inspired blind box offering, the SlideTag. Instead of a mini camera we saw with the Charmera, the SlideTag is equal parts photo display and item tracker, all crammed into a device that dangles off a keychain.
Taking inspiration from the Kodachrome slide mount from the 30s that displays film photos, the SlideTag lets you show off photos on a 1.54-inch e-ink display that can handle six colors and features a whopping 240 x 240 resolution. Much like the Charmera, the SlideTag is a lo-fi version of what you could buy, like a high-resolution digital photo frame or an actual AirTag, but it's a fun combination that has a lot of charm.
If you connect to Kodak's Memory Link app, you can program the SlideTag to display photo galleries and slideshows, or set it up as a to-do list, calendar, timer, QR code and name badge. At 16.6 grams, it's a little heavier than the AirTag, but it still has Bluetooth 5.4 compatibility, an IP54 rating, a replaceable battery and can connect to both Apple's Find My and Google's Find Hub networks.
Kodak is repeating the blind box method for the SlideTag, meaning you'll get one of eight designs, or a much rarer secret edition at a 1 out of 64 chance. The SlideTag is currently available for $35 for a single blind box or $280 for an entire set, but the website has customer orders limited to a max of two blind boxes or one full set.

title_en: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
title_fa: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
excerpt_en: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
excerpt_fa: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
content_en:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.
By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.
Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.
As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.
Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.
